title: Gongura Mutton Curry (Andhra Style Sorrel Mutton Curry)
description: A traditional Andhra-style tangy mutton curry prepared with sorrel leaves (gongura), pressure-cooked tender mutton stock, and robust South Indian spices.
note: CONSISTENCY & HEAT NOTE: Do not cook the mutton on high heat during the final simmer; high heat causes mutton fibers to tighten and become hard. Always maintain a slow-medium flame. If adding extra hot water for more gravy, scale up kari masala accordingly.

items.text: Tomatoes (Large, adjust based on sorrel sourness)

steps.title: Step A: Instant Pot Mutton Stock Pre-Cook
instructions: Add cleaned mutton (1.5 kg), 1.5 cups water, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, red chilli powder, and salt into the Instant Pot.
Lock lid, set valve to Sealing, turn off Keep Warm mode, and pressure cook on High Pressure for 9 minutes.
Quick release steam immediately once the timer finishes. The meat should be ~75% cooked with a rich stock broth. Set aside.

steps.title: Step B: Gongura (Sorrel Leaves) Preparation
instructions: Clean and pluck 1 large bunch of Gongura (sorrel leaves).
Boil the leaves in water until soft and drain the water to reduce excessive sourness. (If the leaves are not very sour, simply sauté them in a dry pan until soft and mushy without boiling).
Lightly mash the cooked sorrel leaves and set aside.

steps.title: Step C: Tempering & Aromatic Base
instructions: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a deep kadai or heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add 1 inch cinnamon stick, 1 tsp fennel seeds (sombu), 1 small bay leaf, 1 star anise, and 1 cardamom pod. Sauté until whole spices pop and release aroma.
Add 1 large chopped red onion. Sauté until translucent and golden brown.
Add 1 large chopped tomato (or 2 small tomatoes, adjusting based on sorrel leaf sourness).
Stir in 1.5 tsp turmeric powder and 2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste. Sauté for 1 minute until raw aromatics dissipate.

steps.title: Step D: Mutton Stock & Spice Integration
instructions: Add the ~75% pre-cooked mutton along with all of its reserved stock broth into the kadai.
Sprinkle in 3 tbsp coriander powder and 3 tbsp mutton / kari masala.
Add the pre-mashed boiled sorrel leaves (Gongura) and stir well to combine.

Reduce heat to slow-medium flame. Simmer gently for 15 to 20 minutes until the mutton transforms from 75% cooked to fully tender and soft. DO NOT cook on high heat, as high heat will make the mutton tough.

dumInstruction: Scatter fresh curry leaves over the gravy and turn off the heat. Consistency Tip: If you prefer more curry or need to adjust consistency while cooking, add hot water and adjust kari masala proportionately to maintain full flavor balance. Serve hot with rice or biryani.
